## Claims
- [proved] Let \(N\ge0\), \(R:\mathbb Z^s\to\mathbb Z^m\), and \(Q=\operatorname{coker}R\). Put \(t=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Q}R\). Smith normal form gives \(U\in\mathrm{GL}_m(\mathbb Z)\), \(V\in\mathrm{GL}_s(\mathbb Z)\), with \(\det U,\det V=\pm1\), such that
  \[
  URV=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_t,0,\ldots,0),\qquad
  1\le d_1\mid\cdots\mid d_t .
  \]
  Therefore
  \[
  Q\cong\bigoplus_{\nu=1}^{t}\mathbb Z/d_\nu\mathbb Z\ \oplus\ \mathbb Z^{m-t}.
  \]
  Hence
  \[
  Q\cong\mathbb Z^N
  \iff t=m-N\ \text{and}\ d_\nu=1\ (1\le\nu\le t).
  \]
  Indeed, under these conditions \(\mathbb Z/d_\nu\mathbb Z=0\), giving \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^{m-t}=\mathbb Z^N\). Conversely, a factor \(d_\nu>1\) supplies nonzero torsion, impossible in \(\mathbb Z^N\), and the free rank is \(m-t=N\). Boundary cases are included: if \(t=0\), the invariant-factor condition is vacuous and \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^m\); if \(m=0\), then \(Q=0=\mathbb Z^0\); if \(N=0\), the criterion requires \(t=m\) and all \(d_\nu=1\), equivalently \(Q=0\).
- [source-backed] With \(q=n-r\), the source identifies \(A:=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) as a quotient whose surviving Schur classes are those indexed by \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\), and states that
  \[
  J_v\subseteq A
  \quad\text{is generated as an ideal by}\quad
  \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq q^r\}.
  \]
  [source-2, lines 1310-1324; source-2, lines 1365-1375]
- [proved] Assume \(1\le i\le q\), \(1\le j\le r\), set \(d_0=ij\), \(D=rq\), and define, for each integer \(d\),
  \[
  B_d:=\{\lambda:\ i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r,\ |\lambda|=d\},
  \qquad m_d:=|B_d|.
  \]
  The degree-\(d\) part of \(J_v\) is
  \[
  (J_v)_d=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in B_d}\mathbb Zs_\lambda.
  \]
  Explicitly, the displayed generators give the inclusion from right to left. Conversely, the Littlewood--Richardson expansion
  \[
  s_\alpha s_\mu=\sum_{\lambda}c_{\alpha\mu}^{\lambda}s_\lambda
  \]
  has \(c_{\alpha\mu}^{\lambda}=0\) unless \(\mu\subseteq\lambda\); thus multiplication of a class containing \(i^j\) produces only classes containing \(i^j\), with classes outside \(q^r\) zero in \(A\). The Schur classes in \(q^r\) are linearly independent, so the sum is direct.
  
  Let
  \[
  T_d:=\{(k,\alpha,\mu):1\le k\le d-d_0,\ 
       \alpha\subseteq q^r,\ |\alpha|=k,\ \mu\in B_{d-k}\},
  \qquad s_d:=|T_d|.
  \]
  Define the integer matrix
  \[
  R_d:\mathbb Z^{s_d}\longrightarrow\mathbb Z^{m_d}
  \]
  using the bases \(T_d\) and \(B_d\), respectively, by
  \[
  (R_d)_{\lambda,(k,\alpha,\mu)}=c_{\alpha\mu}^{\lambda}
  \qquad(\lambda\in B_d).
  \]
  Thus its column indexed by \((k,\alpha,\mu)\) is the Schur-coordinate vector of \(s_\alpha s_\mu\). Since the image of \(\Lambda_+\) in \(A\) is \(A_+\),
  \[
  (\Lambda_+J_v)_d=(A_+J_v)_d=\operatorname{im}R_d,
  \qquad
  (J_v/\Lambda_+J_v)_d\cong\operatorname{coker}R_d.
  \]
  Consequently, for prescribed \(N_d\ge0\),
  \[
  (J_v/\Lambda_+J_v)_d\cong\mathbb Z^{N_d}
  \iff
  \operatorname{rank}R_d=m_d-N_d
  \ \text{and every nonzero Smith factor of }R_d\text{ is }1.
  \]
  For \(d<d_0\) or \(d>D\), \(B_d=T_d=\varnothing\), so \(m_d=s_d=0\), \(R_d:0\to0\), and the quotient degree is \(0\). At \(d=d_0\), \(B_{d_0}=\{i^j\}\), \(T_{d_0}=\varnothing\), and \(R_{d_0}:0\to\mathbb Z\), so the quotient degree is canonically \(\mathbb Z[s_{i^j}]\).
  
  Globally, with
  \[
  R:=\bigoplus_{d=d_0}^{D}R_d,\qquad
  m:=\sum_{d=d_0}^{D}m_d,\qquad
  N:=\sum_{d=d_0}^{D}N_d,
  \]
  one has
  \[
  J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\operatorname{coker}R.
  \]
  Thus the preceding rank-plus-Smith criterion applies to this finite block-diagonal presentation. No ranks or Smith factors for general parameters are asserted here.

## Strategy
Use Schur classes containing \(i^j\) as degreewise columns and all positive-degree Schur multiplications as relation columns; apply Smith normal form separately in each degree.

## Gaps
This certificate supplies the corrected criterion and the exact degreewise presentation, but does not compute \(\operatorname{rank}R_d\) or Smith factors in general.
